fullparsedJSON.title: Generalized Nevo–Peeva conjecture on powers of edge ideals
fullparsedJSON.statement:
Let $G=(V(G),E(G))$ be a finite simple gap-free graph, and let $I(G)$ be its edge ideal. Write $\reg(I(G))$ for its Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity; an ideal has a linear resolution when its graded minimal free resolution is concentrated in one degree.

**Generalized Nevo–Peeva conjecture.** If $\reg(I(G))=n$, then $I(G)^s$ has a linear resolution for all $s\geq n-1$.

The source describes this as a generalization of the Nevo–Peeva conjecture. It is proposed in the paper as a question about when powers of edge ideals of gap-free graphs have linear resolutions, and no resolution status is supplied.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Hiroju Kanno, “Relation between regularity of powers of edge ideals and (im, reg)-invariant extension”, arXiv:2003.05419 (2020).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.05419

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2020).

fullparsedJSON.title: The degree-sensitive density conjecture for 3-flow-critical graphs
fullparsedJSON.statement:
Let $G$ be a **3-flow-critical graph**, meaning that $G$ is bridgeless, does not admit a nowhere-zero $3$-flow, and $G/e$ admits one for every $e\in E(G)$. Let $n=|V(G)|$, let $E(G)$ be its edge set, and let $V_3(G)$ be the set of vertices of degree $3$; write $n_3=|V_3(G)|$.

**Degree-sensitive density conjecture.** For every $3$-flow-critical graph $G$ on $n$ vertices,

$$
|E(G)|<\frac{5}{2}n+n_3.
$$

The authors propose this as a stronger conjecture than the preceding upper-density conjecture and state that it would imply Tutte's $3$-flow conjecture. It is presented as open in the paper.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Jiaao Li, Yulai Ma, Yongtang Shi, Weifan Wang and Yezhou Wu, “On 3-flow-critical graphs”, arXiv:2003.09162 (2020).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.09162

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2020).

fullparsedJSON.title: Partition regularity of the exceptional linear–quadratic equation
fullparsedJSON.statement:
Let $a,b,c$ be non-zero integers, and consider the Diophantine equation

$$
a(x_1^2-x_2^2)=by^2+cz.
$$

**Partition-regularity conjecture.** For every choice of non-zero integers $a,b,c$, this equation is partition regular.

This is the sole exceptional case not covered by the paper's linear–quadratic partition-regularity theorem. The authors state that their lack of knowledge of this case is an artefact of their methods and believe that the cited criterion gives the correct characterisation.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Sean Prendiville, “Counting monochromatic solutions to diagonal Diophantine equations”, arXiv:2003.10161 (2021).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.10161

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2020).

fullparsedJSON.title: The matroid rank conjecture for Hadamard products of linear spaces
fullparsedJSON.statement:
Let $L_1,\dots,L_d \subseteq \mathbb{R}^E$ be finite-dimensional linear spaces, and let $M_1,\dots,M_d$ be their algebraic matroids. Write $r_{M_i}$ for the rank function of $M_i$, and let $\star$ denote the Hadamard product of linear spaces. **Hadamard-product matroid conjecture.**

$$
\mathcal{M}(L_1\star\dots\star L_d)=\mathcal{M}(r_{M_1}+\dots+r_{M_d}-d+1).
$$

This conjecture would generalize the preceding theorem from Hadamard products of two linear spaces to products of an arbitrary finite number of linear spaces. The source does not state a resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Daniel Irving Bernstein, “Generic symmetry-forced infinitesimal rigidity: translations and rotations”, arXiv:2003.10529 (2021).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.10529

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2020).

fullparsedJSON.title: The lower-closure characterization of stably regular triangulations
fullparsedJSON.statement:
Let $P$ be a planar point set, let ${\cal T}_{\mathsf{part}}(P)$ denote its partial triangulations, and let $\mathsf{S}_{\mathsf{triv}}$ be the trivial subdivision. A partial triangulation $T$ is **stably regular** if it is regular for every realization of the order type of $P$.

**Stably regular triangulation conjecture.** A triangulation $T \in {\cal T}_{\mathsf{part}}(P)$ is stably regular if and only if

$$
T \prec^*_1 \mathsf{S}_{\mathsf{triv}}.
$$

The claim proposes an order-type-based characterization of stable regularity, extending the paper's lower-closure criterion. It is presented as a belief about the strongest possible condition based only on the order type, and no resolution is given here.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Uli Wagner and Emo Welzl, “Connectivity of Triangulation Flip Graphs in the Plane”, arXiv:2003.13557 (2020).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.13557

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2020).

fullparsedJSON.title: Kahn's coefficient conjecture for independent sets in regular graphs
fullparsedJSON.statement:
Let $i_k(G)$ be the number of independent sets of size $k$ in a graph $G$. For positive integers $d$ and $n$ with $2d$ dividing $n$, let $H_{d,n}$ be the union of $n/(2d)$ copies of $K_{d,d}$, and let $G$ be a $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices. **Kahn's conjecture.** For every $k$, 
$$
i_k(G)\le i_k(H_{d,n}).
$$
 Kahn's entropy theorem proves the corresponding total-count statement for regular bipartite graphs, and Zhao later resolved the total-count conjecture for all regular graphs; the coefficient-wise assertion remains the stronger conjecture addressed in this paper.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Ewan Davies, Matthew Jenssen and Will Perkins, “A proof of the Upper Matching Conjecture for large graphs”, arXiv:2004.06695 (2021).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.06695

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of April 2020); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

fullparsedJSON.title: Class II augmentation conjecture for a perfect matching
fullparsedJSON.statement: Let $G$ be a graph admitting a perfect matching $M$, and let $G+tM$ denote the multigraph obtained by adding $t$ copies of $M$ to $G$. **Class II augmentation conjecture.** If $G+M$ is Class II, then $G+tM$ is Class II for every positive integer $t$. The claim would imply that a perfect matching cannot require more than one added copy before the resulting multigraph becomes Class I; it is presented without a resolution and remains open.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Edita Máčajová, Giuseppe Mazzuoccolo, Vahan Mkrtchyan and Jean Paul Zerafa, “Some snarks are worse than others”, arXiv:2004.14049 (2020).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.14049

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2020).

fullparsedJSON.title: Balog–Wooley decomposition conjecture
fullparsedJSON.statement:
Let $A$ be a finite subset of $\mathbb{R}$. For a finite set $X$, write

$$
E^+(X)=E_2^+(X),\qquad E^\times(X)=E_2^\times(X),
$$

where $E_k^+(X)=\sum_x r_{X-X}^k(x)$ and $E_k^\times(X)=\sum_x r_{X/X}^k(x)$. Let $\eta\leq 2/3$ be given. **Balog–Wooley conjecture.** For every finite set $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$, there are sets $B,C$ such that $A=B\sqcup C$ and

$$
\max\\{E^+(B),E^\times(C)\\}\lesssim |A|^{3-\eta}.
$$

This decomposition seeks to partition a set into an additively unstructured part and a multiplicatively unstructured part. The source gives no resolution status.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Boqing Xue, “Asymmetric estimates and the sum-product problems”, arXiv:2005.09893 (2020).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.09893

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2020).

fullparsedJSON.title: The necessary-conditions conjecture for super-cyclic bigraphs
fullparsedJSON.statement:
Let $G$ be an $(X,Y)$-bigraph, meaning a bipartite graph with specified ordered bipartition $(X,Y)$. For $A\subseteq X$, define its **super-neighborhood** by

$$
\widehat{N}(A)=\{y\in Y:|N(y)\cap A|\geq 2\}.
$$

The bigraph $G$ is **super-cyclic** if for every $X'\subseteq X$ with $|X'|\geq 3$, it has a cycle $C$ satisfying $V(C)\cap X=X'$. **The super-cyclic bigraph conjecture.** If, for every $A\subseteq X$ with $|A|\geq 3$, one has

$$
|\widehat{N}(A)|\geq |A|
$$

and $G[A\cup\widehat{N}(A)]$ is $2$-connected, then $G$ is super-cyclic. These conditions arise as necessary conditions from a cycle based on each set $A$; the source presents their sufficiency as a conjecture, with no resolution stated.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Alexandr Kostochka, Mikhail Lavrov, Ruth Luo and Dara Zirlin, “Conditions for a bigraph to be super-cyclic”, arXiv:2006.15730 (2020).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.15730

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of June 2020). “Recently, the conjecture was proved in .”

fullparsedJSON.title: Arc-disjoint branchings in 2-arc-strong digraphs of independence number 2
fullparsedJSON.statement: Let $D=(V,A)$ be a digraph. Write $\alpha(D)$ for its independence number, let $\lambda(D)$ denote its arc-connectivity, and let $B_s^+$ and $B_s^-$ denote, respectively, an out-branching and an in-branching rooted at $s$. **Branching conjecture for independence number 2.** Every 2-arc-strong digraph $D$ with $\alpha(D)=2$ has a pair of arc-disjoint branchings $B_s^+,B_s^-$ for every choice of $s\in V$. The source presents this as an open conjecture, alongside a theorem giving a related result for some choice of roots and a 3-arc-strong variant.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Joergen Bang-Jensen, Stéphane Bessy and Anders Yeo, “Non-separating spanning trees and out-branchings in digraphsof independence number 2”, arXiv:2007.02834 (2020).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.02834

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2020). “For instance it is an open problem whether the existence of vertex disjoint paths $P_1,P_2$ such that $P_i$ is an $(s_i,t_i)$-path for $i=1,2$ can be checked in polynomial time (for a partial result see ).”

fullparsedJSON.title: The 3/2 conjecture for triangle covering and packing in random graphs
fullparsedJSON.statement:
Let $G=G(n,m)$ be a random graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges, and let $\tau(G)$ and $\nu(G)$ denote its triangle covering and triangle packing numbers, respectively. For a fixed constant $C>3/2$, consider all values of $m$.

**The 3/2 random-graph conjecture.** For all $C>3/2$ and $G=G(n,m)$, with high probability,

$$
\tau(G)\leq C\cdot\nu(G)
$$

for the full range of $m$.

The conjecture is motivated by estimates suggesting that the ratio $\tau(G)/\nu(G)$ grows from about $1$ when triangles first emerge to about $3/2$ in denser random graphs. The source gives this as a possible direction for future study and provides no resolution.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Patrick Bennett, Ryan Cushman and Andrzej Dudek, “Closing the Random Graph Gap in Tuza's Conjecture Through the Online Triangle Packing Process”, arXiv:2007.04478 (2020).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.04478

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of July 2020). “They demonstrated that for any $\alpha>0$ there are arbitrarily large graphs $G$ of positive density satisfying $\tau(G) > (1-o(1))|G|/2$ and $\nu(G) < (1+\alpha)|G|/4$, disproving a conjecture of Yuster .”

fullparsedJSON.title: Estrada–Rodríguez-Velázquez conjecture on subgraph centrality and walk-regularity
fullparsedJSON.statement: Let $\mathcal{G}=(V,E)$ be a simple undirected graph with adjacency matrix $A$. For $\beta>0$, the $\beta$-subgraph centrality of vertex $i$ is $[e^{\beta A}]_{ii}$, and $\mathcal{G}$ is walk-regular when $[A^r]_{ii}=[A^r]_{jj}$ for all vertices $i,j$ and every positive integer $r$. **Estrada–Rodríguez-Velázquez conjecture.** Given $\beta>0$, a graph $\mathcal{G}$ has all vertices with the same $\beta$-subgraph centrality if and only if $\mathcal{G}$ is walk-regular. The paper proves this for algebraic $\beta$, while the unrestricted statement is not established here.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Francesco Ballini and Nikita Deniskin, “Vertex distinction with subgraph centrality: a proof of Estrada's conjecture and some generalizations”, arXiv:2007.08956 (2021).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.08956

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of July 2020). “Some counterexamples for the closeness and betweenness centralities were found independently by Rombach and Porter and by Stevanovi\'c , but the conjecture remained open for degree and eigenvector centralities.”

fullparsedJSON.title: Conjecture on exponential diagonal equality for non-diagonalizable directed graphs
fullparsedJSON.statement:
Let $A$ be the adjacency matrix of a directed, unweighted graph, and assume that $A$ is non-diagonalizable. Let $i$ and $j$ be vertices, and let $\beta\in\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$. **Exponential diagonal equality conjecture.** If

$$
[e^{\beta A}]_{ii}=[e^{\beta A}]_{jj},
$$

then, for every integer $r>0$,

$$
[A^r]_{ii}=[A^r]_{jj}.
$$

This would extend the proposition proved in the paper from a restricted Jordan-form situation to all non-diagonalizable adjacency matrices; the source gives no resolution.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Francesco Ballini and Nikita Deniskin, “Vertex distinction with subgraph centrality: a proof of Estrada's conjecture and some generalizations”, arXiv:2007.08956 (2021).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.08956

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of July 2020). “Some counterexamples for the closeness and betweenness centralities were found independently by Rombach and Porter and by Stevanovi\'c , but the conjecture remained open for degree and eigenvector centralities.”

fullparsedJSON.title: Conjecture that line graphs of $e$-positive spiders are $e$-positive
fullparsedJSON.statement:
Let $S$ be a spider, and let $S_L$ denote its line graph, whose vertices correspond to the edges of $S$ and whose adjacency records incidence of edges in $S$. A graph is **$e$-positive** when its chromatic symmetric function is a nonnegative linear combination of elementary symmetric functions.

**Line-graph conjecture.** If a spider $S$ is $e$-positive, then its line graph $S_L$ is $e$-positive.

The source notes that this holds for all $e$-positive spiders known to the authors, but gives no proof in general. The conjecture is also motivated by the relationship between connected partitions of a spider and of its line graph.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Kai Zheng, “On the e-positivity of trees and spiders”, arXiv:2008.05038 (2022).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.05038

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2020).

fullparsedJSON.title: Stronger tail-restricted growth conjecture for power-free languages
fullparsedJSON.statement:
For a real $b2>1$, let $b1'(k,b2)$ be the growth rate of the language of words containing no $b2$-power whose tail has length at most $2$. **Stronger tail-restricted growth conjecture.** For every fixed integer $ngeq2$ and arbitrarily large integer $k$,

$$
\alpha'\left(k,\frac{n}{n-1}\right)=k+1-n-\frac{n-1}{k}+O\left(\frac{1}{k^2}\right)
$$

and

$$
\alpha'\left(k,\frac{n}{n-1}^+\right)=k+2-n-\frac{n-1}{k}+O\left(\frac{1}{k^2}\right).
$$

The authors describe this as a probably stronger conjecture and report only progress toward the main conjecture; no resolution is given.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Matthieu Rosenfeld, “Lower-bounds on the growth of power-free languages over large alphabets”, arXiv:2008.05192 (2021).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.05192

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2020).

fullparsedJSON.title: Brubach–Sankararaman–Srinivasan–Xu sampling conjecture for hypergraph matchings
fullparsedJSON.statement:
Let $H=(V,E)$ be a hypergraph, let $w\in\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^E$ be edge weights, and let $x\in[0,1]^E$ be a fractional matching, meaning that

$$
\sum_{e\in\delta(v)}x(e)\leq 1\qquad\text{for every }v\in V,
$$

where $\delta(v)=\\{e\in E:v\in e\\}$. **Brubach–Sankararaman–Srinivasan–Xu conjecture.** It is possible to efficiently sample a matching $M\subseteq E$ from a distribution such that every edge $e\in E$ satisfies

$$
\Pr[e\in M]\geq\frac{x(e)}{|e|-1+\frac{1}{|e|}}.
$$

This is a distributional and algorithmic strengthening of the Füredi–Kahn–Seymour guarantee. The source describes related weaker bounds and states that the conjecture remains unresolved.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Georg Anegg, Haris Angelidakis and Rico Zenklusen, “Simpler and Stronger Approaches for Non-Uniform Hypergraph Matching and the Füredi, Kahn, and Seymour Conjecture”, arXiv:2009.00697 (2020).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.00697

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2020). “Even though the conjecture remains open, par\-tial progress has been achieved in several directions.”

fullparsedJSON.title: The Latin-square repair conjecture
fullparsedJSON.statement:
Let $k,\ell\in\mathbb N$ and let $A\in\mathcal{R}(k,\ell)$. For a Latin square $L$ of order $n$, let $t(A,L)$ denote the density of copies of $A$ in $L$.

**Latin-square repair conjecture.** For every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $\delta>0$ such that, if $t(A,L)<\delta$, then one can modify entries of $L$ on at most $\varepsilon n^2$ positions and obtain a Latin square $L'$ with $t(A,L')=0$.

This is a stronger form of the removal lemma because it preserves the Latin-square condition rather than deleting entries. The source presents it as a possible stronger result, and gives no evidence of resolution.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Frederik Garbe, Robert Hancock, Jan Hladký and Maryam Sharifzadeh, “Limits of Latin squares”, arXiv:2010.07854 (2023).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.07854

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2020).

fullparsedJSON.title: The cyclomatic-number bound for the difference between metric dimensions
fullparsedJSON.statement:
Let $G\ne K_{2}$ be a graph with cyclomatic number $c$, defined by $c=|E(G)|-|V(G)|+1$. Here, $\dim(G)$ and $\operatorname{edim}(G)$ denote the vertex and edge metric dimensions of $G$, respectively.

**Cyclomatic-number bound.** For every such graph,

$$
\left\vert \dim(G)-\operatorname{edim}(G)\right\vert \leq c.
$$

The bound is motivated by the corresponding equality for trees other than $K_{2}$ and by the established result for unicyclic graphs. The claim proposes the analogous bound for graphs with higher cyclomatic number; the paper presents it as an ongoing conjectural direction.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Jelena Sedlar and Riste Škrekovski, “Bounds on metric dimensions of graphs with edge disjoint cycles”, arXiv:2010.10326 (2020).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.10326

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2020).

fullparsedJSON.title: Induced subgraph isomorphism hardness conjecture for bipartite permutation graphs
fullparsedJSON.statement:
Let $\mathcal X$ be a hereditary subclass of bipartite permutation graphs. The **induced subgraph isomorphism problem** asks whether an input graph occurs as an induced subgraph of another input graph.

**Induced subgraph isomorphism hardness conjecture.** Unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$, the induced subgraph isomorphism problem is NP-hard in $\mathcal X$ if and only if $\mathcal X$ contains all linear forests. Equivalently, for every fixed $k$, the problem can be solved in polynomial time for $P_k$-free bipartite permutation graphs.

The conjecture would characterize the hereditary subclasses of bipartite permutation graphs on which induced subgraph isomorphism is NP-hard, with linear forests as the unique minimal hard class.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Bogdan Alecu, Vadim Lozin and Dmitriy Malyshev, “Critical properties of bipartite permutation graphs”, arXiv:2010.14467 (2020).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.14467

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2020).

fullparsedJSON.title: Converse of the balancedness criterion for regular staged trees
fullparsedJSON.statement: Let a staged tree be **regular** when, for every pair of vertices in the same stage and every pair of outgoing edges, the corresponding subtree monomials satisfy the required equality of cross-products. Let it be **balanced** when these cross-product identities hold for every such pair of vertices and edges. **Converse of the balancedness criterion.** All regular staged trees are balanced. The paper states that this converse holds for all binary trees with three levels; whether it holds for regular staged trees in the stated generality is left as an open question.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Christiane Görgen, Manuele Leonelli and Orlando Marigliano, “The curved exponential family of a staged tree”, arXiv:2010.15515 (2022).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.15515

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2020).
